```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(biscale)

census_hh   <- read_csv(here::here("data", "census_households_hackney.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)
overlap     <- read_rds(here::here("data", "overlap.rds"))
# Numbers used in text on the Overview and page 4
lsoa_df   <- st_drop_geometry(overlap$lsoa)
n_hot_old <- sum(lsoa_df$bi_class == "3-3")

share_by_heat <- lsoa_df |>
  group_by(heat_band) |>
  summarise(n = sum(aged_75plus)) |>
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n) * 100))

share_cool <- share_by_heat$share[share_by_heat$heat_band == "Lowest third"]
share_hot  <- share_by_heat$share[share_by_heat$heat_band == "Highest third"]
who_latest  <- read_rds(here::here("data", "who_latest.rds"))
hackney_col <- "#C8553D"
bi_palette  <- "BlueOr"   # bivariate palette for page 4's map and legend
who_trend   <- read_rds(here::here("data", "who_trend.rds"))
who_trend_gaps <- read_rds(here::here("data", "who_trend_gaps.rds"))
dementia_dx <- read_rds(here::here("data", "dementia_dx_london.rds"))
where_lsoa  <- read_rds(here::here("data", "where_lsoa.rds"))
where_df    <- st_drop_geometry(where_lsoa)   # for the scatters
hot_days    <- read_rds(here::here("data", "hot_days.rds"))
```

## Row {height="60%"}
::: {.card title="Who is at risk"}
Hackney has lower recorded rates of coronary heart disease, hypertension, diabetes and dementia than the London average, which fits its young population, but among London's highest recorded rates of depression and serious mental illness.

[See who is at risk](#who-is-at-risk)
:::

::: {.card title="Where it's hot"}
Hackney's hottest neighbourhoods are its least leafy, not its most deprived. Since 1990, every decade has had more days above 25°C than any decade before it.

[See where it's hot](#where-its-hot)
:::

::: {.card title="Where they overlap"}
Older residents lean slightly towards Hackney's cooler neighbourhoods: `r share_cool`% of residents aged 75+ live in its coolest third and `r share_hot`% in its hottest. `r n_hot_old` neighbourhoods are in both its hottest and oldest thirds.

[See where they overlap](#where-they-overlap)
:::

## Row

### Column {.tabset width="60%"}

::: {.card title="Latest"}

```{r}
#| label: who-latest
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(who_latest, aes(x = value, y = fct_rev(area), colour = area)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ short_label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3,
             labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 24)) +  expand_limits(x = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    n.breaks = 3,
    labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%", drop0trailing = TRUE),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))
  ) +  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(Hackney = hackney_col, London = "grey60", England = "grey60"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing    = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 15, 5, 5)
  )
```

Panels named after a condition show the share of GP-registered patients with that diagnosis. These rates are crude (not age-standardised), so Hackney's young population lowers them.

Social contact is from 2019/20, the latest year with a Hackney value.

:::

::: {.card title="Over time"}
```{r}
#| label: who-trend
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 6
who_trend |>
  # Reverse so England and London are drawn first and Hackney sits on top
  mutate(area = fct_rev(area)) |>
  arrange(area) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, colour = area,
             group = interaction(series, area))) +
  geom_segment(
    data = who_trend_gaps,
    aes(x = year, xend = next_year, y = value, yend = next_value,
        linetype = "Year with no value"),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ short_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3,
             labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 24)) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    n.breaks = 3,
    labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%", drop0trailing = TRUE),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(Hackney = hackney_col, London = "grey45", England = "grey75"),
    breaks = c("Hackney", "London", "England")   # legend order
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Year with no value" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  guides(linetype = guide_legend(position = "inside")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position        = "top",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.75, 0.13),
    panel.grid.minor       = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing          = unit(1.2, "lines")
  )
```

Recorded depression rises partly because the register counts adults diagnosed since April 2006, so the window keeps lengthening. NHS Digital warns that 2020/21 GP figures may be inaccurate.

Age has no trend because it comes from a single census. Dashed lines join the years either side of a missing value. Social contact has none for 2020/21, when the survey was voluntary because of COVID; depression has none for 2023/24 in the source data.
:::

::: {.card title="Table"}
```{r}
#| label: who-table
# England's value for each row, to sit beside Hackney's
england_values <- who_latest |>
  filter(area == "England") |>
  select(short_label, england = value)

who_latest |>
  filter(area == "Hackney") |>
  left_join(england_values, by = "short_label") |>
  arrange(short_label) |>
  transmute(short_label, period,
            hackney = value, england,
            compared_england = coalesce(compared_england, "–"),
            recent_trend     = coalesce(recent_trend, "–")) |>
  mutate(across(c(hackney, england),
                scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1, suffix = "%"))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Indicator", "Period", "Hackney", "England",
                             "Compared with England", "Recent trend"),
               align = "llrrll")
```

Residents aged 75+ is from Census 2021, so it has no comparison or trend. Prevalence figures are crude GP-recorded rates. Fingertips judges only some indicators against England; "Not compared" means it makes no judgement, and a percentage after a judgement is the confidence level it used. Recent trend is Fingertips' own test of Hackney's values, so it can differ from how a line looks on the Over time tab.
:::

### Column {width="40%"}

::: {.card title="Is Hackney’s dementia diagnosis rate unusual for London?"}

```{r}
#| label: dementia-dx
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 6
dx_band    <- filter(dementia_dx$band, level == "95")
dx_hackney <- filter(dementia_dx$points, is_hackney)
dx_extremes <- filter(dementia_dx$points, value %in% range(value))

ggplot(dementia_dx$points,
       aes(x = value, y = fct_reorder(area_name, value))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = dx_band$lower, xmax = dx_band$upper,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey92") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = dementia_dx$london_avg, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = is_hackney), size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(data = dx_hackney, aes(label = area_name),
            colour = hackney_col, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -3.5, size = 4) +
  geom_text(data = dx_extremes, aes(label = area_name),
            colour = "grey30", hjust = 1, nudge_x = -2, size = 3.5) +
  expand_limits(x = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = hackney_col, `FALSE` = "grey60"),
                      guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
  )
```

Each dot is a London borough; the line is the London average and the shaded band is the range boroughs typically fall within, not a confidence interval. The rate is diagnosed patients aged 65+ as a share of the estimated number living with dementia, so higher is better. The lowest, the City of London, has an estimated 89 people with dementia, so its rate is far less certain than other boroughs’.


:::

## Row {height="20%"}

::: {.card title="Reading this page"}
The lines through the dots on the Latest tab are 95% intervals, the range of underlying rates consistent with each figure; most are hidden behind the dots because chance makes little difference in populations this large. The shaded band on the diagnosis rate chart is the range London boroughs typically fall within, so a borough outside it differs more than boroughs usually do.
:::

# Where it's hot

## Row {height="70%"}

### Column {width="60%"}

::: {.card title="Hackney's hottest neighbourhoods are its least leafy, not its most deprived"}
```{r}
#| label: where-map
# One colour scale per layer
pal_lst    <- colorNumeric("YlOrRd", domain = where_lsoa$lst)
pal_canopy <- colorNumeric("Greens", domain = where_lsoa$tree_canopy)

# Hover label: readable name, then the three values
hover <- sprintf(
  "<strong>%s (%s)</strong><br>Surface temperature: %.1f°C<br>Tree cover: %.0f%%<br>Deprivation: decile %d of 10 (1 = most deprived)",
  where_lsoa$msoa_hcl_name,
  str_sub(where_lsoa$lsoa_name, -4),
  where_lsoa$lst,
  where_lsoa$tree_canopy,
  where_lsoa$imd_decile
) |>
  lapply(htmltools::HTML)

leaflet(where_lsoa) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addPolygons(
    group = "Surface temperature",
    fillColor = ~pal_lst(lst), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 0.5,
    label = hover,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "#333333",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addPolygons(
    group = "Tree cover",
    fillColor = ~pal_canopy(tree_canopy), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 0.5,
    label = hover,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "#333333",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("Surface temperature", "Tree cover"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) |>
  addLegend(pal = pal_lst, values = ~lst, opacity = 0.8,
            title = "Surface<br>temperature",
            labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "°C"),
            position = "bottomright",
            className = "info legend legend-lst") |>
  addLegend(pal = pal_canopy, values = ~tree_canopy, opacity = 0.8,
            title = "Tree cover",
            labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "%"),
            position = "bottomright",
            className = "info legend legend-canopy") |>
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
    function(el, x) {
      // Legends may not exist yet (leaflet waits until page 3 is visible),
      // so mark the map with the selected layer and let CSS do the hiding
      this.on('baselayerchange', function(e) {
        el.classList.toggle('show-canopy', e.name === 'Tree cover');
      });
    }
  ")
```

Satellites measure how hot surfaces get, not the air people feel, and Landsat passes in the late morning, before the afternoon peak. Tree cover data are from 2013.
:::

### Column {.tabset width="40%"}
::: {.card title="Deprivation" fill = "false"}
Surface temperature barely changes with deprivation: Hackney's most and least deprived neighbourhoods run about as hot.

```{r}
#| label: where-deprivation
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4

# Shared base for both tabs: same points, temperature axis and theme
lst_scatter <- ggplot(where_df, aes(y = lst)) +
  geom_point(colour = hackney_col, alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "°C")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = "Deprivation score") + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

lst_scatter +
  aes(x = imd_score) +
  expand_limits(x = 0)

```

Higher scores are more deprived. Most Hackney neighbourhoods are in England's most deprived 40%, but scores still run from 3 to 61, so a link would show if there were one.
:::

::: {.card title="Tree cover" fill="false"}
Neighbourhoods with more tree cover have cooler surfaces.

```{r}
#| label: where-tree-cover
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4
lst_scatter +
  aes(x = tree_canopy) +
  expand_limits(x = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = "Share of area under tree canopy") 
```

Tree cover data are from 2013. Leafy neighbourhoods often contain parks, so part of the cooling may come from the park as a whole, not only its trees.
:::

## Row {height="30%"}

::: {.card title="Is Hackney getting more hot days?"}
```{r}
#| label: where-hot-days
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 1.5
ggplot(hot_days, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = days), fill = hackney_col, alpha = 0.3, width = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_10y), colour = hackney_col, linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(10),
                     expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 3,
                     labels = scales::label_number(suffix = " days"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

Each column is a year's days above 25°C, and the line is a 10-year average, so it starts in 1940. These are air temperatures, not surface temperatures, and end in 2025.
:::

# Where they overlap

## Row

### Column {width="70%"}

::: {.card title="Where do hot neighbourhoods and older residents coincide?"}
```{r}
#| label: overlap-map
lsoa    <- overlap$lsoa
bi_cols <- bi_pal(bi_palette, dim = 3, preview = FALSE)

# Hover for each LSOA, flagging care homes because their residents raise the 75+ share
care_txt <- if_else(lsoa$n_care_homes > 0,
                    "<br>Has a care home; its residents are counted here", "")

hover <- sprintf(
  "<strong>%s (%s)</strong><br>Surface temperature: %.1f°C (%s in Hackney)<br>Aged 75+: %.1f%%, %d residents (%s in Hackney)%s",
  lsoa$msoa_hcl_name, str_sub(lsoa$lsoa_name, -4),
  lsoa$lst, tolower(lsoa$heat_band),
  lsoa$share_75plus, lsoa$aged_75plus, tolower(lsoa$age_band),
  care_txt
) |>
  lapply(htmltools::HTML)

care_hover <- sprintf("<strong>%s</strong><br>Care home",
                      overlap$care_homes$name) |>
  lapply(htmltools::HTML)

cool_hover <- sprintf("<strong>%s</strong><br>Cool space<br>%s",
                      overlap$cool_spaces$name,
                      overlap$cool_spaces$opening_hours) |>
  lapply(htmltools::HTML)

leaflet(lsoa) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addMapPane("points", zIndex = 450) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = unname(bi_cols[lsoa$bi_class]), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 0.5,
    label = hover,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "#333333",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    data = overlap$care_homes, group = "Care homes",
    radius = 6, color = "white", weight = 1.5, opacity = 1,
    fillColor = "#333333", fillOpacity = 1,
    label = care_hover,
    options = pathOptions(pane = "points")
  ) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    data = overlap$cool_spaces, group = "Cool spaces",
    radius = 6, color = "#333333", weight = 2, opacity = 1,
    fillColor = "white", fillOpacity = 1,
    label = cool_hover,
    options = pathOptions(pane = "points")
  ) |>
  addLayersControl(
    overlayGroups = c("Care homes", "Cool spaces"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  )
```

This shows where hot neighbourhoods and older residents coincide, not which residents are actually exposed. Care homes are from the CQC directory (October 2026); cool spaces are the nine indoor sites on the GLA's 2025 map, and parks aren't included.
:::

### Column {width="30%"}

::: {.card title="How to read the map" fill="false"}
```{r}
#| label: overlap-legend
#| fig-width: 3.5
#| fig-height: 3.5
lsoa_df   <- st_drop_geometry(overlap$lsoa)
n_hot_old <- sum(lsoa_df$bi_class == "3-3")
hot_min   <- round(min(lsoa_df$lst[lsoa_df$heat_band == "Highest third"]), 1)
old_min   <- round(min(lsoa_df$share_75plus[lsoa_df$age_band == "Highest third"]), 1)

bi_legend(pal = bi_palette, dim = 3,
          xlab = "Hotter", ylab = "More aged 75+",
          size = 12)

share_by_heat <- lsoa_df |>
  group_by(heat_band) |>
  summarise(n = sum(aged_75plus)) |>
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n) * 100))

share_cool <- share_by_heat$share[share_by_heat$heat_band == "Lowest third"]
share_hot  <- share_by_heat$share[share_by_heat$heat_band == "Highest third"]
```

The darkest colour marks the `r n_hot_old` neighbourhoods in both Hackney's hottest third and its oldest third. Both are relative to the rest of Hackney: the hottest third starts at `r hot_min`°C, and the oldest third at `r old_min`% of residents aged 75+. `r share_cool`% of residents aged 75+ live in Hackney's coolest third and `r share_hot`% in its hottest, and the gap holds without the neighbourhoods that have a care home.

Solid dark circles are care homes; white circles are cool spaces.
:::

# Data and methods

## Row {.tabset height="85%"}

::: {.card title="Sources"}

| Source | What it gives | Period | Geography | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OHID Fingertips | GP-recorded prevalence, dementia diagnosis rate, social contact | Varies by indicator | Borough | Open Government Licence |
| Census 2021 (Nomis) | Age, older people living alone | 2021 | LSOA | Open Government Licence |

Remaining rows from the plan's data sources table go here.
:::

::: {.card title="Methods"}
**Confidence intervals.** What the 95% interval means, in two or three sentences.

**Funnel plots and overdispersion.** How the limits are drawn, why they're widened, and why only two indicators get a funnel.

**Crude rates.** Why GP prevalence isn't age-standardised, and what that means in a young borough.

**Surface temperature.** Which Landsat summer was used, how it's averaged to LSOAs, and that it measures surfaces rather than air.

**Bivariate bands.** How the three bands are drawn across Hackney's LSOAs.

**Change of data source.** Fingertips is being replaced by Find public health data; which one this dashboard uses.
:::

::: {.card title="Limitations"}
**Who is at risk**

- **Crude rates.** One sentence.
- **GP registers count diagnoses.** One sentence.
- **Evidence comes from elsewhere.** One sentence.

**Where it's hot and where they overlap**

- **Surface, not air, temperature.** One sentence.
- **Old tree cover data.** One sentence.
- **Bands are relative to Hackney.** One sentence.
- **Care homes in Census counts.** One sentence.
- **Ecological fallacy.** One sentence.

**What's missing**

- **No indoor overheating data.** One sentence.
- **No local heat death figures.** One sentence.
:::
